scope: Whole-book identity proposal; modern rendering owned here is Chapters 1–11 only. Later original source evidence was read only for identity facts, not edited or rendered.
coordinateBasis: 1-based chapter and paragraph positions in the pinned 34-chapter original-en; decorative scene-break blocks excluded as recorded in SOURCE.md.

characters.name: Mr. Lockwood
characters.role: Tenant at Thrushcross Grange and the outer narrator.
characters.identityRule: No first name is supplied. His report of another person is not that person’s independent testimony.

characters.name: Ellen “Nelly” Dean
characters.role: Housekeeper, former nurse and principal retrospective narrator.
characters.identityRule: All these names denote one woman. Do not merge her with Zillah. Treat “my mistress” and “my master” as contextual references, never her aliases.

characters.name: Heathcliff
characters.role: The child brought into the Earnshaw household, later Lockwood’s landlord.
characters.identityRule: Heathcliff is both given name and surname (4:38). Do not invent an Earnshaw surname or confirmed ancestry. Distinguish the deceased Earnshaw child whose name he receives and his own son Linton Heathcliff.

characters.name: Catherine Earnshaw — elder Catherine
characters.role: Hindley’s sister; the elder Catherine in Nelly’s history.
characters.identityRule: Catherine Linton is her married name and is also her daughter’s birth name. Bare Cathy/Catherine requires time and speaker context. “Catherine Heathcliff” scratched at 3:4 is a name she imagines, not evidence that she marries Heathcliff. The child at the window in Lockwood’s dream is associated with her without confirming a supernatural event.

characters.name: Catherine “Cathy” Linton — younger Catherine
characters.role: Edgar and the elder Catherine’s daughter; the young Mrs. Heathcliff in the opening frame.
characters.identityRule: Separate identity from her mother. First appears unnamed in 2:9; identification is explained in 4:15. Mrs. Heathcliff can instead mean Isabella in earlier events. Later name/relationship reveals must be unlocked in reading order, not inferred from chapter number alone across frame and flashback.

characters.name: Hindley Earnshaw
characters.role: The elder Catherine’s brother and Hareton’s father.
characters.identityRule: Mr. Earnshaw means his father in the early childhood history and usually Hindley after Chapter V. Never attach every Earnshaw or “master” mention to Hindley.

characters.name: Hareton Earnshaw
characters.role: Hindley and Frances’s son; Nelly’s childhood charge.
characters.identityRule: The living man at 2:52 is not the person named in the 1500 carving at 1:11. Childhood and adult appearances are one identity. Bare Earnshaw and Mr. Earnshaw require context.

characters.name: Edgar Linton
characters.role: Isabella’s brother, raised at Thrushcross Grange.
characters.identityRule: Do not merge with his father, also Mr. Linton, or his nephew Linton Heathcliff. “Master Linton” in the early scenes can mean young Edgar; it is not a safe global alias for the later boy.

characters.name: Isabella Linton
characters.identityRule: Mrs. Heathcliff denotes Isabella in one part of the past and the younger Catherine in the opening frame. “Isabel” at 11:38 is a variant, not a new person. Gate marriage and parentage details to their narrative revelation.

characters.name: Linton Heathcliff
characters.identityRule: Linton is his given name, not Edgar’s surname used for the same man. His naming and birth are disclosed at 17:66. Keep this identity distinct from his father; do not expose later relationships at the book’s opening.

characters.name: Joseph
characters.identityRule: Keep readable Yorkshire grammar and vocabulary in his dialogue. Do not invent a surname or identify the servant with biblical names used in his speech.

characters.name: Frances Earnshaw
characters.identityRule: Mrs. Earnshaw can instead denote Hindley’s mother in the earlier history. No birth surname or detailed background is supplied.

characters.name: Mr. Earnshaw — elder
characters.role: Father of Hindley and the elder Catherine; brings Heathcliff home from Liverpool.
characters.identityRule: No first name supplied. Do not confuse with Hindley or Hareton. His care for Heathcliff does not establish biological paternity.

characters.name: Mrs. Earnshaw — elder
characters.role: Mother of Hindley and the elder Catherine.
characters.identityRule: Separate from Frances. No first name supplied; a shared married title is not sufficient for identity resolution.

characters.name: Mr. Linton — elder
characters.identityRule: Distinct from Edgar. Do not infer a first name. His later absence does not make every earlier Mr. Linton reference Edgar.

characters.name: Mrs. Linton — elder
characters.role: Mother of Edgar and Isabella; addressed as Mary in 6:8.
characters.identityRule: Distinct from Catherine Earnshaw after her marriage. Use Mary only in that supported address, not as a general bare-word automatic trigger.

characters.name: Mr. Kenneth
characters.identityRule: The generic “doctor” is context-dependent. No first name supplied. His period medical claims remain character speech, not editorial guidance.

characters.name: Zillah
characters.role: Housekeeper at Wuthering Heights in Lockwood’s opening visits.
characters.identityRule: Separate from Nelly Dean, the Grange housekeeper. Lockwood initially identifies her by appearance rather than name.

characters.name: Mr. Shielders
characters.role: The curate named in Mr. Linton’s account of the children’s upbringing.
characters.identityRule: Do not automatically assign every curate or parson across all periods to Shielders. Distinguish him from the dream preacher Jabez Branderham.

ambiguousNames.decision: Resolve through generation, narrator and story time; never merge the mother and daughter.
The opening young widow is the younger Catherine. Nelly’s past account also uses this married title for Isabella.
Resolve given name versus family surname and the generation being narrated.
Resolve the person, period and household position rather than applying one global replacement.
Use family relationships and period to distinguish the two women.
These titles span generations and must not be assigned without local context.

nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.name: Hareton Earnshaw in the 1500 carving
nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.decision: An inscribed historical name; not the living Hareton. No inferred biography or exact family relationship.

nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.name: The deceased Earnshaw child called Heathcliff
nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.decision: A separate child recalled when the foundling receives his name; do not merge with the main character.

nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.name: Reverend Jabez Branderham
nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.decision: The sermon title and Lockwood’s dream preacher; not the parish curate Shielders.

nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.name: Catherine at the window
nonHouseholdOrInsetReferences.decision: Keep within Lockwood’s dream account. Do not label the narrator’s supernatural interpretation as established fact or create a third Catherine.

spoilerPolicy: Opening cast states only early identifying relationships and positions. Runtime cards must unlock later biography in reading order, accounting for the 1801 frame and flashbacks. No imported full-plot biographies.
integrationRequirements: Treat IDs as proposed book-scoped identities, not registered global IDs.
Review ambiguous aliases manually before generating runtime cards.
Reconcile wh1 dialect and naming policy with the other rendering sessions.
Do not turn characters/ into narration roles or initiate audio generation.
